newsitem.title: UK: Guardian Royal off 4 pct after block trade. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Guardian Royal off 4 pct after block trade. [CORRECTED 16:50 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Guardian Royal Exchange Plc hit a two-month low after a large block trade (corrects from agency cross trade) and amid more attractive earnings results from other composite insurers, market sources said.
By 1437 GMT, Guardian Royal stock was down 12-1/2p at 276p on volume of 23.7 million, the most active in the FTSE 100.
The sell side of the block trade was for 11.3 million shares at 271p, of which 11 million were sold on again at 273p, market sources said.
One analyst blamed Guardian's drop on strong operating performances from other insurers, though he said Guardian looked "exceptionally cheap" at the moment.
"The fundamental problem...is that the insurance market in the short to medium term is going to have a bumpy road," he said, citing industry overcapacity and falling premium rates.
Shares in Commercial Union Plc rose 2-1/2p to 740p, Royal and Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc lost 3p to 533p and General Accident Plc fell 7p to 935-1/2p.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
